turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack with a raised eyebrow whether he intended to live at 149 Belgrave Square himself or merely rent it to another lady of advanced years.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen insisted that her engagement to Jack should not be contingent on his address or financial status and asked her mother to consider his character instead.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen firmly that social standing and financial stability were prerequisites for marriage, and that considering character alone would be imprudent.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen insisted that her mother reconsider her stance, arguing that love and compatibility were more important than material wealth and social standing.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen sternly that while love and compatibility were indeed desirable, they were secondary to the practicalities of a stable and respectable marriage.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother defiantly that she would not let societal norms dictate her happiness and that she loved Jack for who he was, not for his bank account or address.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that her sentiments, while touching, were impractical and would lead to ruin. She insisted that Gwendolen must marry someone who could provide her with the life to which she was entitled.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not be swayed by practical considerations when her heart was involved and that she would marry Jack regardless of societal expectations.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen firmly that her defiance would not alter the fact that she was expected to marry a man of her own class and standing, someone who could offer her the stability and respectability she deserved.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother that she would not be coerced into marriage and that her heart was set on Jack, regardless of what society deemed suitable.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen sternly that her heart had no place in the matter of marriage and that she must consider the propriety and financial security of her potential husband above all else.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen insisted that her heart would not be silenced and that she would marry Jack, no matter what her mother decreed.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen with a stern gaze that she would not tolerate such insubordination and that she must choose a husband who met the expectations of their social class, not some upstart.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother defiantly that she would not be swayed by her social expectations and that her heart was already pledged to Jack.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen with an icy tone that she would not permit such a match and that she expected her daughter to find a suitable husband from within their own social circle.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Gwendolen told her mother with a fierce determination that she would not be dictated to and that she would marry Jack despite her mother’s disapproval.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell with a respectful but firm tone that he understood her concerns and would do everything in his power to prove himself a worthy suitor for Gwendolen.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack with a stern and unyielding tone that she would not condone such a match and that he must demonstrate his worthiness to her standards before she would consider him suitable for her daughter.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he would respect her wishes and work diligently to meet her expectations, hoping to earn her approval and Gwendolen’s happiness.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack with a condescending smile that she would be watching his every move and that any deviation from the proper conduct expected of a gentleman of his standing would not be tolerated.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell that she was engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen that she was not engaged to anyone and that when she did become engaged, she or her father would inform her of the fact.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Gwendolen told Lady Bracknell, 'Mamma!'

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to go to the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Gwendolen to get into the carriage.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack to take a seat.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he preferred standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she felt bound to inform him that he was not down on her list of eligible young men.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he must admit he smoked.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was glad to hear it and that a man should always have an occupation of some kind.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he was twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if he knew everything or nothing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he knew nothing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she was pleased to hear it and that she did not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell asked Jack if his income was in land or in investments.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that his income was in investments.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that it was satisfactory.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he had a country house with some land attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that a country house was satisfactory and asked how many bedrooms it had.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that he owned a house in Belgrave Square, but it was let by the year to Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that she did not know Lady Bloxham.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that Lady Bloxham went about very little and was a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bracknell told Jack that nowadays that was no guarantee of respectability of character and asked what number in Belgrave Square.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Jack told Lady Bracknell that the number was 149.
